glosses: The act of striking the palms of the hands, or any two surfaces, together.

examples.text: He summoned the waiter with a clap.

glosses: The explosive sound of thunder.

examples.text: The deafening claps of thunder and the dazzling flashes of lightning which lit up the ghastly scene testified that the artillery of heaven had lent its supernatural pomp to the already gruesome spectacle.
With each clap of thunder echoing from one high building to another the noise was terrific.

glosses: Any loud, sudden, explosive sound made by striking hard surfaces together, or resembling such a sound.

examples.text: Off in the distance, he heard the clap of thunder.
Give the door such a clap, as you go out, as will shake the whole room.

glosses: A slap with the hand, usually in a jovial manner.

examples.text: His father's affection never went further than a handshake or a clap on the shoulder.

glosses: A single, sudden act or motion; a stroke; a blow.

examples.text: What, fifty of my followers at a clap!

glosses: To strike the palms of the hands together, creating a sharp sound.

examples.text: The children began to clap in time with the music.

glosses: To applaud.

examples.text: The audience loudly clapped the actress, who responded with a deep curtsey.

glosses: To slap with the hand in a jovial manner.

examples.text: He would often clap his teammates on the back for encouragement.

examples.text: He clapped the empty glass down on the table.

glosses: To slam (a door or window); formerly often construed with to.

glosses: To create or assemble (something) hastily (usually followed by up or together).
